توج منتخب حلب بطلاً لبطولة سوريا الأولى: The Aleppo national team was crowned champion of the first Syrian mini-football championship after defeating the Daraa national team on penalties, 3-2, in the final match that was held on Monday, February 16, after regular time ended in a 3-3 draw. The match witnessed strong competition and exchange of goals between the teams The teams were elected during regular time, before heading to penalty kicks to decide the result, according to what the Ministry of Sports and Youth published through its official accounts. The Aleppo national team started the match by leading by three goals to one, before the tables were adjusted after their goalkeeper was sent off in the 70th minute of the match. The Daraa team took advantage of the numerical deficiency and reduced the gap, before achieving the equalizer in the last seconds of stoppage time, so the two teams resorted to penalty kicks, which the Aleppo team decided in their favor with a score of (3-2). The Aleppo national team added individual awards to the collective achievement, as its striker, Mohamed Darwish, won He was named the tournament's top scorer after scoring 8 goals, while goalkeeper Mohamed Maery won the F-Award Award.
